weeks.development: The fertilized egg has implanted in the uterus, and the basic layers that will form your baby are starting to develop.
A simple heart tube is forming and will soon start to beat.
The heart begins to beat, and tiny buds that will become arms and legs appear.
The brain and face are developing quickly, and small hand buds are visible.
Fingers are starting to form, and the beginnings of eyes and ears are visible.
All major organs have begun to form, and the embryo is starting to look more baby-shaped.
Fingers and toes are separating, and bones are starting to harden.
Your baby is now officially called a fetus. Fingernails are starting to form.
Reflexes are developing, with small movements beginning that you cannot feel yet.
Vocal cords are forming, and fingerprints are starting to develop.
Your baby can make facial expressions, and the neck is more defined.
Bones are getting stronger, and light sensitivity is starting to develop.
Your baby's ears are in their final position, picking up sound as vibration.
Your baby is laying down fat stores, and the skeleton is hardening.
Your baby can hear some sounds now, like your heartbeat and voice.
A protective waxy coating (vernix) is forming on your baby's skin.
You're halfway there. Your baby is swallowing more and practicing breathing movements.
Your baby's movements are growing stronger as muscles keep developing.
Your baby's senses of touch and taste are developing further.
Blood vessels in the lungs are developing to prepare for breathing air.
Your baby's face is almost fully formed, and taste buds are developing.
Your baby is putting on more baby fat and starting to look less wrinkled.
Your baby's eyes are developing the ability to open and respond to light and sound.
Your baby is settling into more regular sleeping and waking cycles.
Your baby can blink, and eyelashes have grown in.
Your baby's bones are fully formed but still soft and flexible.
Your baby is gaining weight quickly, and the brain is developing fast.
Your baby can turn their head and is practicing sucking.
Your baby's fingernails have reached their fingertips.
Your baby's bones are hardening, except the skull, which stays soft to help with birth.
Your baby's fingernails are fully grown, and the skin is becoming smoother.
Your baby's kidneys are fully developed, and the liver is starting to process waste.
Your baby is likely settling into a head-down position to get ready for birth.
Your baby is considered "early term" — organs are mature enough to function on their own.
Your baby is practicing small movements like grasping, in preparation for birth.
Your baby is considered full term. The brain and lungs keep maturing even now.
Your due date has arrived — many babies arrive within two weeks before or after this date.
